In mathematics, more specifically in the context of [[geometric quantization]], '''quantization commutes with reduction''' states that the space of global sections of a line bundle ''L'' satisfying the quantization condition<ref>This means that the [[curvature form|curvature]] of the connection on the line bundle is the symplectic form.</ref> on the [[symplectic quotient]] of a compact [[symplectic manifold]] is the space of invariant [[section (fiber bundle)|sections]]{{vague|reason=Invariant under what? Sections on which the symplectic form is invariant?|date=February 2019}} of ''L''.

This was conjectured in 1980s by Guillemin and Sternberg and was proven in 1990s by Meinrenken<ref>{{harvnb|Meinrenken|1996}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Meinrenken|1998}}</ref> (the second paper used [[symplectic cut]]) as well as Tian and Zhang.<ref>{{harvnb|Tian|Zhang|1998}}</ref> For the formulation due to Teleman, see C. Woodward's notes.
